q: Why does a balancer without feedback multiply an outage?
a: It keeps feeding the dying backend its full share, so those requests all fail while healthy capacity idles.

q: What do closed, open, and half-open mean?
a: Closed flows and counts failures; open ejects until cooldown; half-open sends one trial to detect recovery.

q: Does a breaker heal the backend?
a: No. It bounds the bleeding and holds p99; only the fix or new capacity restores it. Under persistent failure it flaps by design.

q: Breakers react to traffic failures — what finds failures traffic hasn't hit?
a: Active health probes on a tick; the half-open trial here is the probe until the engine grows ticks.
